subject: Architecture
title: Suspension Bridges: Hanging by Cables
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Suspension Bridges: Hanging by Cables.

hook.text: Suspension bridges hang from cables — the deck literally floats between towers on strands of steel wire.

buildup.text: Main cables drape between tall towers. Vertical suspender cables connect the main cables to the deck below.

discovery.text: Each main cable contains thousands of individual wires — bundled together, they can support enormous loads.

twist.text: Suspension bridges are flexible by design. In strong wind, the deck sways several feet side to side.

climax.text: The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge in Japan has the world's longest span — 6,532 feet of suspended roadway.

punchline.text: Steel wires thinner than pencils hold up a mile of highway.

quiz.question: What is the world's longest suspension bridge span?
options: The Golden Gate Bridge at 4,200 feet
The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge at 6,532 feet

details.summary: Suspension bridges hang their roadway from vertical cables attached to massive main cables draped between tall towers. The main cables transfer loads to anchorages at each end through pure tension, enabling spans exceeding 2,000 meters — the longest of any bridge type.
details.whyItMatters: Suspension bridges conquered distances once thought unbridgeable. By using high-strength cables in tension rather than rigid beams, they achieve spans that would be impossible with any other structural system.
takeaways: Roadway hangs from cables draped between tall towers
Main cables work in pure tension, anchored at each end
They achieve the longest spans of any bridge type

faq.question: How are suspension bridge cables made?
faq.answer: Individual steel wires are spun back and forth between anchorages by traveling wheels, then compacted and wrapped into massive bundles. The Golden Gate Bridge's two main cables each contain 27,572 individual wires totaling over 129,000 kilometers of wire.

faq.question: What is the longest suspension bridge?
faq.answer: The 1915 Çanakkale Bridge in Turkey, completed in 2022, has a main span of 2,023 meters. The Akashi Kaikyo Bridge in Japan held the record for 24 years at 1,991 meters. Even longer spans are being planned using advanced materials.
